ai.title: The US let Nvidia sell chips to an empty office in China
ai.brief: The government is approving sales of Nvidia’s AI chips to Chinese firms with ties to blacklisted companies. The government is approving sales of Nvidia’s AI chips to Chinese firms with ties to blacklisted companies. Concerns are being raised that neither the Commerce Department nor Nvidia are doing their due diligence when it comes to vetting Chinese firms cleared to handle the company’s H200 AI chips. ” In fact, the paper could find little evidence that the company exists in any meaningful way: What little information can be found about New Matrix is concerning. Its owners have ties to a Chinese private equity firm that has been blacklisted by the US government since 2024. And according to the Times , this is not a rare lapse in oversight, but a troubling pattern of companies connected to entities with national-security-related trade restrictions being approved to purchase Nvidia chips.

sec.title: Hackers pull off $133 million French bank heist via service provider
sec.brief: French cooperative bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa was targeted in a cyberattack that enabled fraudulent transactions of up to $133 million, forcing it to respond by suspending certain systems. The bank says that the attacker used its own account to initiate transactions to other banking organizations, but customer assets remain unaffected. 5 billion euros in assets. Reports about the incident emerged on November 2, initially from blockchain fraud investigator ZachXBT, who warned of a large-scale unauthorized withdrawal from multiple centralized exchange accounts occurring a day earlier. According to the investigator, the attacker may have stolen up to 118 million euros ($133 million) and withdrawn it as USDC and USDT stablecoins. At the time, ZachXBT did not name the entity but said that the lack of public disclosure allowed the attacker to launder $30 million by November 3, which EU law enforcement would otherwise have frozen.
